units.left_text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
units.right_text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

units.left_text: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
units.right_text: “Futility of futilities,”

units.left_text: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
units.right_text: What does a man gain from all his labor,

units.left_text: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
units.right_text: Generations come and generations go,

units.left_text: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
units.right_text: The sun rises and the sun sets;

units.left_text: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
units.right_text: The wind blows southward,

units.left_text: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
units.right_text: All the rivers flow into the sea,

units.left_text: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
units.right_text: All things are wearisome,

units.left_text: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.
units.right_text: What has been will be again,

units.left_text: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
units.right_text: Is there a case where one can say,

units.left_text: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
units.right_text: There is no remembrance

units.left_text: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
units.right_text: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

units.left_text: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
units.right_text: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a miserable task God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!

units.left_text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
units.right_text: What is crooked cannot be straightened,

units.left_text: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
units.right_text: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”

units.left_text: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
units.right_text: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow,

units.left_text: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.
units.right_text: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!”

units.left_text: I said of laughter, “It is foolishness;” and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”
units.right_text: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”

units.left_text: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their lives.
units.right_text: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly— my mind still guiding me with wisdom— until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

units.left_text: I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.
units.right_text: I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.

units.left_text: I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit.
units.right_text: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.

units.left_text: I made myself pools of water, to water the forest where trees were grown.
units.right_text: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.

units.left_text: I bought male servants and female servants, and had servants born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all who were before me in Jerusalem.
units.right_text: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,

units.left_text: I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men: musical instruments of all sorts.
units.right_text: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men — many concubines.

units.left_text: So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.
units.right_text: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.

units.left_text: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
units.right_text: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.

units.left_text: Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
units.right_text: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.

units.left_text: I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly; for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which has been done long ago.
units.right_text: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?

units.left_text: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
units.right_text: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:

units.left_text: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness—and yet I perceived that one event happens to them all.
units.right_text: The wise man has eyes in his head,

units.left_text: Then I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
units.right_text: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?”

units.left_text: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no memory forever, since in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the wise man must die just like the fool!
units.right_text: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!

units.left_text: So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
units.right_text: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.

units.left_text: Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all of my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
units.right_text: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.

units.left_text: Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.
units.right_text: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.

units.left_text: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with skillfulness; yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
units.right_text: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.

units.left_text: For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?
units.right_text: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?

units.left_text: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail is grief; yes, even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
units.right_text: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.

units.left_text: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
units.right_text: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.

units.left_text: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
units.right_text: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?

units.left_text: For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
units.right_text: To everything there is a season,

units.left_text: a time to be born,
units.right_text: a time to be born and a time to die,

units.left_text: a time to kill,
units.right_text: a time to kill and a time to heal,

units.left_text: a time to weep,
units.right_text: a time to weep and a time to laugh,

units.left_text: a time to cast away stones,
units.right_text: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together,

units.left_text: a time to seek,
units.right_text: a time to search and a time to count as lost,

units.left_text: a time to tear,
units.right_text: a time to tear and a time to mend,

units.left_text: a time to love,
units.right_text: a time to love and a time to hate,

units.left_text: What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?
units.right_text: What does the worker gain from his toil?

units.left_text: I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
units.right_text: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.

units.left_text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
units.right_text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.

units.left_text: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
units.right_text: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,

units.left_text: Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
units.right_text: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor — this is the gift of God.

units.left_text: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
units.right_text: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.

units.left_text: That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago. God seeks again that which is passed away.
units.right_text: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.

units.left_text: Moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
units.right_text: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.

units.left_text: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
units.right_text: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”

units.left_text: I said in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals.
units.right_text: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”

units.left_text: For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals, for all is vanity.
units.right_text: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other — they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.

units.left_text: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
units.right_text: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.

units.left_text: Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
units.right_text: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?

units.left_text: Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who can bring him to see what will be after him?
units.right_text: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?

units.left_text: Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
units.right_text: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.

units.left_text: Therefore I praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive.
units.right_text: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.

units.left_text: Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
units.right_text: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

units.left_text: Then I saw all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
units.right_text: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.
units.right_text: The fool folds his hands

units.left_text: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
units.right_text: Better one handful with tranquility

units.left_text: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.
units.right_text: Again, I saw futility under the sun.

units.left_text: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
units.right_text: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile — a miserable task.

units.left_text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
units.right_text: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.

units.left_text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
units.right_text: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

units.left_text: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
units.right_text: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?

units.left_text: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
units.right_text: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

units.left_text: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn’t know how to receive admonition any more.
units.right_text: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.

units.left_text: For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
units.right_text: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.

units.left_text: I saw all the living who walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.
units.right_text: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.

units.left_text: There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was—yet those who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
units.right_text: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

units.left_text: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
units.right_text: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.

units.left_text: For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words.
units.right_text: As a dream comes through many cares,

units.left_text: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
units.right_text: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.

units.left_text: It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
units.right_text: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.

units.left_text: Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
units.right_text: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?

units.left_text: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words; but you must fear God.
units.right_text: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.

units.left_text: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter, for one official is eyed by a higher one, and there are officials over them.
units.right_text: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.

units.left_text: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
units.right_text: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

units.left_text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
units.right_text: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.

units.left_text: When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
units.right_text: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?

units.left_text: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
units.right_text: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.

units.left_text: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
units.right_text: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,

units.left_text: Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
units.right_text: or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.

units.left_text: As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
units.right_text: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.

units.left_text: This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
units.right_text: This too is a grievous affliction: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?

units.left_text: All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
units.right_text: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.

units.left_text: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
units.right_text: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him — for this is his lot.

units.left_text: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
units.right_text: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.

units.left_text: For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life, because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
units.right_text: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.

units.left_text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:
units.right_text: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

units.left_text: a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
units.right_text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.

units.left_text: If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he;
units.right_text: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

units.left_text: for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
units.right_text: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.

units.left_text: Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other.
units.right_text: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,

units.left_text: Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place?
units.right_text: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

units.left_text: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
units.right_text: All a man’s labor is for his mouth,

units.left_text: For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?
units.right_text: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?

units.left_text: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
units.right_text: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

units.left_text: Whatever has been, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is mightier than he.
units.right_text: Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.

units.left_text: For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
units.right_text: For the more words, the more futility — and how does that profit anyone?

units.left_text: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?
units.right_text: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?

units.left_text: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
units.right_text: A good name is better than fine perfume,

units.left_text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
units.right_text: It is better to enter a house of mourning

units.left_text: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
units.right_text: Sorrow is better than laughter,

units.left_text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
units.right_text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning,

units.left_text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
units.right_text: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke

units.left_text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
units.right_text: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot,

units.left_text: Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
units.right_text: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool,

units.left_text: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning.
units.right_text: The end of a matter is better than the beginning,

units.left_text: Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
units.right_text: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit,

units.left_text: Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
units.right_text: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?”

units.left_text: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
units.right_text: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good,

units.left_text: For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
units.right_text: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter,

units.left_text: Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight which he has made crooked?
units.right_text: Consider the work of God:

units.left_text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
units.right_text: In the day of prosperity, be joyful,

units.left_text: All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
units.right_text: In my futile life I have seen both of these:

units.left_text: Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
units.right_text: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

units.left_text: Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
units.right_text: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?

units.left_text: It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also don’t withdraw your hand from that; for he who fears God will come out of them all.
units.right_text: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.

units.left_text: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
units.right_text: Wisdom makes the wise man

units.left_text: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn’t sin.
units.right_text: Surely there is no righteous man on earth

units.left_text: Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
units.right_text: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.

units.left_text: for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
units.right_text: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.

units.left_text: All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise;” but it was far from me.
units.right_text: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.

units.left_text: That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
units.right_text: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?

units.left_text: I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
units.right_text: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.

units.left_text: I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
units.right_text: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.

units.left_text: “Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find an explanation
units.right_text: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.

units.left_text: which my soul still seeks, but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all those.
units.right_text: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.

units.left_text: Behold, I have only found this: that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions.”
units.right_text: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”

units.left_text: Who is like the wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
units.right_text: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.

units.left_text: I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
units.right_text: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.

units.left_text: Don’t be hasty to go out of his presence. Don’t persist in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him,
units.right_text: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.

units.left_text: for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
units.right_text: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”

units.left_text: Whoever keeps the commandment shall not come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure.
units.right_text: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.

units.left_text: For there is a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him.
units.right_text: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.

units.left_text: For he doesn’t know that which will be; for who can tell him how it will be?
units.right_text: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?

units.left_text: There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver those who practice it.
units.right_text: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.

units.left_text: All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every work that is done under the sun. There is a time in which one man has power over another to his hurt.
units.right_text: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.

units.left_text: So I saw the wicked buried. Indeed they came also from holiness. They went and were forgotten in the city where they did this. This also is vanity.
units.right_text: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.

units.left_text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
units.right_text: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.

units.left_text: Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.
units.right_text: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.

units.left_text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow, because he doesn’t fear God.
units.right_text: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.

units.left_text: There is a vanity which is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
units.right_text: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.

units.left_text: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
units.right_text: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.

units.left_text: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (even though eyes see no sleep day or night),
units.right_text: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth — though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night —

units.left_text: then I saw all the work of God, that man can’t find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he won’t find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won’t be able to find it.
units.right_text: I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.

units.left_text: For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it is love or hatred, man doesn’t know it; all is before them.
units.right_text: So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.

units.left_text: All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him who sacrifices, and to him who doesn’t sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; he who takes an oath, as he who fears an oath.
units.right_text: It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.

units.left_text: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all. Yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
units.right_text: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.

units.left_text: For to him who is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
units.right_text: There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.

units.left_text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead don’t know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten.
units.right_text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

units.left_text: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy has perished long ago; neither do they any longer have a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
units.right_text: Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.

units.left_text: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works.
units.right_text: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

units.left_text: Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil.
units.right_text: Let your garments always be white,

units.left_text: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity, for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun.
units.right_text: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun — all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

units.left_text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
units.right_text: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

units.left_text: I returned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
units.right_text: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

units.left_text: For man also doesn’t know his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them.
units.right_text: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.

units.left_text: I have also seen wisdom under the sun in this way, and it seemed great to me.
units.right_text: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:

units.left_text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
units.right_text: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.

units.left_text: Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
units.right_text: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.

units.left_text: Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
units.right_text: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”

units.left_text: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
units.right_text: The calm words of the wise are heeded

units.left_text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
units.right_text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war,

units.left_text: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor;
units.right_text: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil,

units.left_text: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand,
units.right_text: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right,

units.left_text: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
units.right_text: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking,

units.left_text: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
units.right_text: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post,

units.left_text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
units.right_text: There is an evil I have seen under the sun —

units.left_text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
units.right_text: Folly is appointed to great heights,

units.left_text: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
units.right_text: I have seen slaves on horseback,

units.left_text: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
units.right_text: He who digs a pit may fall into it,

units.left_text: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.
units.right_text: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them,

units.left_text: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
units.right_text: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened,

units.left_text: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
units.right_text: If the snake bites before it is charmed,

units.left_text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
units.right_text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious,

units.left_text: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
units.right_text: The beginning of his talk is folly,

units.left_text: A fool also multiplies words.
units.right_text: Yet the fool multiplies words.

units.left_text: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
units.right_text: The toil of a fool wearies him,

units.left_text: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child,
units.right_text: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth,

units.left_text: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles,
units.right_text: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles,

units.left_text: By slothfulness the roof sinks in;
units.right_text: Through laziness the roof caves in,

units.left_text: A feast is made for laughter,
units.right_text: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry,

units.left_text: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts;
units.right_text: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts,

units.left_text: Cast your bread on the waters;
units.right_text: Cast your bread upon the waters,

units.left_text: Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight;
units.right_text: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight,

units.left_text: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth;
units.right_text: If the clouds are full,

units.left_text: He who observes the wind won’t sow;
units.right_text: He who watches the wind will fail to sow,

units.left_text: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind,
units.right_text: As you do not know the path of the wind,

units.left_text: In the morning sow your seed,
units.right_text: Sow your seed in the morning,

units.left_text: Truly the light is sweet,
units.right_text: Light is sweet,

units.left_text: Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all;
units.right_text: So if a man lives many years,

units.left_text: Rejoice, young man, in your youth,
units.right_text: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young,

units.left_text: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart,
units.right_text: So banish sorrow from your heart,

units.left_text: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth,
units.right_text: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,

units.left_text: Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened,
units.right_text: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened,

units.left_text: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble,
units.right_text: on the day the keepers of the house tremble

units.left_text: and the doors shall be shut in the street;
units.right_text: when the doors to the street are shut

units.left_text: yes, they shall be afraid of heights,
units.right_text: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road,

units.left_text: before the silver cord is severed,
units.right_text: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped

units.left_text: and the dust returns to the earth as it was,
units.right_text: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came

units.left_text: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher.
units.right_text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher.

units.left_text: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
units.right_text: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.

units.left_text: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
units.right_text: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.

units.left_text: The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
units.right_text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.

units.left_text: Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
units.right_text: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.

units.left_text: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
units.right_text: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.

units.left_text: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
units.right_text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
